messages:
kai: Heads-up - I hit a weird onboarding failure: quickstart will suddenly trigger a torrent of page requests when the auth token swaps and the paginator prefetch is enabled. 429s follow even though server quota is unchanged.

mira: Can you paste a short repro? which quickstart flags? node or py?

kai: Node quickstart. Run with --concurrency=10 and PREFETCH=3, then run a tiny script that rotates the local auth token every ~1.8s. Repro script: 
```bash
# start quickstart
./start-quickstart --concurrency=10 &
# rotate token in background
while true; do sleep 1.8; ./rotate-local-token.sh; done
```

kai: Logs show the same cursor refetched multiple times after a refresh: 
```
[2026-05-02T15:03:02Z] INFO paginator fetch cursor=21 attempt=1
[2026-05-02T15:03:03Z] WARN auth: rotating token acct=team-x
[2026-05-02T15:03:03Z] ERROR http 401 -> retry
[2026-05-02T15:03:03Z] INFO paginator fetch cursor=21 attempt=2
[2026-05-02T15:03:03Z] INFO paginator fetch cursor=22 attempt=1
[2026-05-02T15:03:04Z] ERROR http 429 rate_limit
```

mira: That pattern looks like two problems stacked: (1) prefetch multiplies in-flight cursors, (2) the retry path after auth refresh spawns new requests instead of reusing the inflight promise. Node's paginator used to attach retries to the original request but that changed in the middleware refactor.

oliver: Interesting edge: on the client we track an in-memory `rateMeter` with a window estimate. Node resets the window when auth refresh event fires which causes a temporary refill; combined with prefetch you can suddenly send a lot of tokens. Py preserves remainder which smooths it out.

sylvie: So parity gaps: inflight dedupe + window reset semantics. Both amplify under pagination+prefetch. New users copy quickstart and see server 429s and open tickets.

mira: Immediate mitigation suggestions?

kai: For quickstart: set PREFETCH=1, reduce concurrency to 4, and set REFRESH_JITTER_MS=200 in the sampleenv. That makes it much less likely to spike.

oliver: I'll add a toggle `ATTACH_RETRY_TO_INFLIGHT=true` in node-sdk that will reattach retry promises to existing inflight cursor promises. Also add `preserve_window_on_refresh=true` default in SDK config.

sylvie: For onboarding docs let's add a short note under "Rate limits & pagination" that explains prefetch tradeoffs and token-rotation interactions. Also include the quickstart-safe env example.

mira: Can we add a lightweight integration test in devex CI that simulates token rotation during pagination so we catch regressions? e.g., spin a fake token provider that rotates and assert no duplicate fetches per cursor id and no sudden window refills.

oliver: Yep - test plan: run quickstart in CI with PREFETCH=3, force token rotate, assert duplicates >1 are seen (failing test), then run with ATTACH_RETRY_TO_INFLIGHT=true and expect zero duplicates and stable rateMeter. Will commit both negative and positive test cases.

kai: I opened a tiny reproducer repo gist and a CI step link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex-repro/tree/paginate-rotations (WIP)

devx-bot: Created issue #4477: "quickstart: pagination + token rotations -> duplicate requests & 429s" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/issues/4477)

devx-bot: Opened PR #920: "node: attach retries to inflight paginator promises + preserve_window_on_refresh default" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/920)

mira: Awesome. Let's also surface this in the SDK parity doc with a short table: Node: attach_retries=false (legacy), Python: attach_retries=true, Go: attach_retries=true; window_on_refresh: Node=reset, Py=preserve, Go=preserve (old bug fixed). That will help support and users understand differences.

sylvie: After PR lands, we should flip quickstart defaults to PREFETCH=1 and add a short blurb in the README. I'll open a follow-up PR to samples repo to update the quickstart template and onboarding docs.

kai: Verified locally with the PR branch - duplicates gone and 429 spikes reduced. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

mira: Closing here, tracking work in GH. Follow ups in #4477 and PR threads.
